industrial discharges containing non biodegradble soluble organic matter were not treated effectively in the WWTP and that these discharges were a major factor in decreasing biodegradability.

the non biodegradable fraction of the wastewater organic compounds is a major factor in decreasing the biodegradability and the fate of wastewater in a biological WWT, and that the COD fractionation method and fluorescence spectroscopy can be used to quantify the non biodegraded fraction of wastewater organic matter and to examine the ultimate fate of organic matter.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the characteristics of wastewater organic matter contained by industrial discharges and their fate in a biological WWTT.
the biodegradable fraction of wastewater organic matter, rather than a specific group of chemicals, and the fate of the organic matter in a WWTP.
the characteristics and bioreactivity of the wastewater organic matters contained in industrial wastewater and the fate of these matters in the biological WWTP.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the industrial discharge that contained the non biodegradable fraction of wastewater organic matter was a significant factor in the decrease of biodegradability and in the decrease of the removal efficiency of the wastewater organic in the biological WWTPs.

industrial discharge containing nonbiodegradable soluble organic matters was the most important factor in decreasing the biodegradability and the ultimate fate of the wastewater organic matters in a biological WWTT.

the industrial discharges that contained nonbiodegradable soluble organic matters were the main cause of the reduction of biodegradability in the biological WWTPs, and thus the industrial discharge should be treated separately from domestic wastewater.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the industrial discharge that contains a large amount of soluble COD, which is not biodegraded by biological processes in the conventional biological wastewater treatment plants, should be treated by other advanced processes, such as membrane bioreactors, or should be discharged to a separate treatment plant, to prevent the decrease in bioreactor performance and the increase in effluent soluble COD.
the industrial discharge that contains non biodegradable COD should be pretreated before it is discharged into a biological WWTP.
industrial discharges containing a large amount of biodegradable soluble COD are treated effectively in a conventional biological wastewater treatment plant.
The main takeaway from our work is that
wastewater organic matter in the biological WWTPs in Korea is not homogeneously biodegradable, but is composed of various fractions of biodegradable and biodegradable organic substances.

industrial discharge containing nonbiodegradable soluble organic carbon can escape from a biological WWTP and that the industrial discharges should be treated separately from domestic wastewater in a biological WWT.
the biodegradability, and hence the treatability of wastewater organic matter, can be predicted by analyzing the soluble organic matter fraction.
